references.text: Jacob's blessing of Joseph also mentions the blessings of heaven from above and the blessings of the deep that lie beneath, reflecting the same themes of fertility and abundance.
Isaac's blessing of Jacob includes the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth, paralleling the blessing with dew from heaven in Moses' blessing of Joseph.
The continuation of the blessing over Joseph elaborates on the precious gifts from heaven, the earth, and the mountains.
Tehom (the deep) mentioned here is the same word used in the creation account for the primeval deep, referring to water sources beneath the earth.
The psalm describes how God waters the mountains from his lofty chambers and satisfies the earth with fruit, reflecting the theme of heavenly blessings.
The dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion mentions dew as a symbol of blessing, similar to the dew mentioned in the blessing over Joseph.
